newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Lace up after rescheduling share allocation.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Lace up after rescheduling share allocation.

text.p: Shares of Nippon Lace Co Ltd rose sharply on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) in Tuesday morning trade after the company announced it had rescheduled the third-party allocation of new shares.
By 0140 GMT, Nippon Lace was up 25 yen, or 10.20 percent, at 270. It was the largest percentage gainer in the first section of the TSE.
Nippon Lace, a Japanese lace manufacturer, said on Monday it would go ahead in early April with a plan for a third-party allocation of new shares that had been cancelled last week.
It will issue six million new shares at 280 yen per share to two investors to whom it had originally planned to allocate the new shares, Nippon Lace said in a statement.
The payment date will be April 7, the lace maker said.
The company said in February that it would issue six million new shares at 590 yen per share in a third-party allocation, but on March 11 it cancelled its original plan due to a fall in share prices.
